decisions.question: S108 found nidana.model.4's scope cannot analyze: it lands topology-ir@v1's TopologyDefinition with its factory and getters, which name TransformEdge, and the plan lands TransformEdge, EdgeInput, TopicInput, StageInput, CombinatorKind and FunctionRef at nidana.model.5. How is it fixed?

options.label: Re-plan the unshipped nidana.model.4 and .5 through hsdd-phase-plan: .4 lands the whole main library (topology-dsl@v2 and topology-ir@v1's IR and Function references sections), .5 lands topology_ir.dart; reconcile rewrites topology-ir@v1's Delivery paragraph
options.consequence: The plan states what the phases can do; the split follows the two public libraries; consumer edges still wait on .5; two governance steps and a re-run switch before .4's plan.

options.label: Rule that .4's implementers land the types its signatures name, leaving the plan text as it is
options.consequence: No governance step, but the node plan, .4's and .5's contexts and topology-ir@v1's Delivery paragraph would all misstate where declarations land, and a phase would be deviating from its plan by order of the controller.

options.label: Land TopologyDefinition without its factory and getters at .4
options.consequence: Breaks D3 (a type-level phase lands the declarations its contract's Interface states) and the scope's own words.

decisions.chosen: Re-plan the unshipped nidana.model.4 and .5 through hsdd-phase-plan: .4 lands the whole main library (topology-dsl@v2 and topology-ir@v1's IR and Function references sections), .5 lands topology_ir.dart; reconcile rewrites topology-ir@v1's Delivery paragraph
decisions.why: Governance changes only through its owning skill, and the phase context's Discipline says a plan that is wrong mid-phase goes back to the root; the intake segment re-planned unshipped phases in place the same way (S86, S92). A Dart declaration cannot name an undeclared type, so the closure of TopologyDefinition's signatures must land with it; the main library holds exactly that closure, which makes the split principled rather than ad hoc.
